page.layout: One printed page (right page of the opening). Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Main text in one column, with a centred small heading "Explicatio 2." in the middle. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot. No marginal notes on this page. The left-edge fragments on the scan belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: Qvatuor igitur exercitus Tartaro-rum versus omnes mundi plagas e-ruperunt, unus in Orientem atq; Si-nam; alter in Indiam; tertius in Per-siam; qvartus in ipsam Europam.
main_text.head: Explicatio 2.
main_text.p: Exercitus igitur Tartarorum Oc-cidentalium sub Duce Batku universa Russiam, Hungariam, Austriam, Poloniam & Silesiam vastavit, ac maxi-mô præliô Henricum Ducem Sile-siæ superavit. Hi Tartari vastissimum regnum condidere, quod vocabatur Desthense, i.e. Tartaria deserta; cu-jus Regibus tota Russia parebat. Alio nomine dicebatur Zavothense, quod trans Volgam, ad mare Caspium, situm erat. Hoc regnum destruxit circa A.C. 14co[?] Tamerlanes: ex cuius ruinis emerserunt regna Ca-san, Astracan, &c, quod hodieque famosissimum est, Crimense sive Præ-copense.

page.notes: The numeral in "A.C. 14co" is printed with lowercase o's in place of zeros; copied as printed with [?]. "Ca-san" is read from the long-s form and is slightly uncertain. Italic words are set in italic type in the scan. The catchword "Se-" appears at the lower right below the last line. Printed "Desthense" and "Zavothense" are as printed and may be misprints for Tartarian place names, left unchanged.
